turns.answer:
For a 12-hour winter power outage, I recommend a portable power station with 2,000–3,000 Wh of battery capacity, a pure sine wave inverter, and at least 1,500 W of AC output.

My first choice would be the EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max for a typical pellet stove. If your stove uses more electricity, or you want extra runtime in freezing weather, consider a 3,000 Wh model.

The important distinction is that a pellet stove needs electricity for its auger, combustion fan, circulation blower, and ignition system. It doesn't usually need 1,500 W continuously, but it does need enough energy to run all night.

Winter outage precautions

Keep the battery indoors at a safe operating temperature, choose pure sine wave output, and verify the stove's power-loss and restart requirements. Some power stations have UPS/EPS transfer modes, but a transfer time specification alone does not guarantee your stove will stay running. Test the setup before an outage.

One question that will determine the right model: What brand and model is your pellet stove (Harman, Quadra-Fire, Englander, PelPro, etc.)?

With that, I can narrow down whether a 2,000 Wh station is sufficient or you really need 3,000 Wh for 12 hours.
